---
title: "Visualizing the Weibull Distribution"
author: "Anthony Morciglio"
date: "11/11/2025"
output: html_document
---

```{r weibull-distribution, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# -----------------------------------------------------------
# Title: Weibull Distribution Example
# Description:
# This code illustrates the Weibull Distribution for the example
# given in the blog post. We define the Weibull PDF and CDF for
# shape parameter k = 2.5 and scale parameter λ = 1000.
#
# The Weibull distribution is often used to model lifetimes or
# failure times in reliability engineering. By plotting both the
# PDF and CDF, we visualize how the distribution behaves and how
# probabilities accumulate over time.
#
# The plots show:
#   - The PDF (density function), which represents the likelihood
#     of failure at a specific time.
#   - The CDF, which represents the probability that failure
#     occurs before a given time.
# -----------------------------------------------------------

# Load necessary library
library(ggplot2)

# Define parameters
shape_k <- 2.5   # shape parameter
scale_l <- 1000  # scale parameter

# Create a sequence of x values (time or lifetime)
x <- seq(0, 2000, length.out = 400)

# Compute the Weibull PDF and CDF
pdf_vals <- dweibull(x, shape = shape_k, scale = scale_l)
cdf_vals <- pweibull(x, shape = shape_k, scale = scale_l)

# Create a combined data frame for plotting
weibull_df <- data.frame(x = x, PDF = pdf_vals, CDF = cdf_vals)

# Plot 1: Probability Density Function (PDF)
pdf_plot <- ggplot(weibull_df, aes(x = x, y = PDF)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue", size = 1.2) +
  labs(title = paste0("Weibull Probability Density Function (k = ", shape_k, ", λ = ", scale_l, ")"),
       x = "Lifetime (hours)",
       y = "Density") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))

# Plot 2: Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF)
cdf_plot <- ggplot(weibull_df, aes(x = x, y = CDF)) +
  geom_line(color = "red", size = 1.2) +
  labs(title = paste0("Weibull Cumulative Distribution Function (k = ", shape_k, ", λ = ", scale_l, ")"),
       x = "Lifetime (hours)",
       y = "Cumulative Probability") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))

# Display both plots
pdf_plot
cdf_plot

# Compute an example probability:
# Probability that a light bulb fails before 800 hours
x_val <- 800
prob_failure <- pweibull(x_val, shape = shape_k, scale = scale_l)
cat("Probability that a light bulb fails before 800 hours (P(X < 800)) =", round(prob_failure, 3), "\n")
```
